about.title: Personal Injury Help in Montclair, California
about.longDescription: Montclair sits at a busy crossroads of San Bernardino County, where daily traffic on Central Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, Holt Boulevard, and the I-10 freeway keeps the city moving — and occasionally leads to collisions. Public records show 234 injury collisions in the most recent final year, with 348 people hurt and 1 traffic death. Many of these crashes happen on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and shoppers converge near the freeway on-ramps and shopping corridors. If you were injured in one of these incidents, or in a fall, workplace accident, or other mishap around town, you may be weighing medical bills, missed work, and an uncertain path forward. We handle personal injury claims for Montclair residents and can review your case at no cost. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and gives you direct access to an attorney who can evaluate your specific situation.

items.title: Your Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover a share of damages. We can help sort out how fault is divided in your specific crash.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Suffered
items.desc: For most ordinary injury cases in California, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited before your case is even evaluated.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. That structure lets you focus on recovery instead of worrying about legal bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Montclair?
items.answer: California law generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public property, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated altogether.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Montclair?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes of reported crashes along Central Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, Holt Boulevard, and near the I-10 freeway, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing the most activity. These are simply neutral counts from public data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe money if I contact you?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review at no cost to you. Our team works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are personal injury attorneys serving Montclair and San Bernardino County. We handle injury cases directly and can evaluate your situation at no cost.
